body.statement: If \(W_1,W_2,\ldots\) are independent and identically distributed random vectors in a fixed finite-dimensional Euclidean space, \(\mathbb E W_1=0\), and \(\mathbb E\|W_1\|^2<\infty\), then \(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^nW_i\) converges in distribution to the centered multivariate normal law with covariance \(\mathbb E(W_1W_1^{\mathsf T})\), allowing a singular covariance matrix.

source.verbatim_statement: Suppose that for every n the random vectors Y_{n,1}, ..., Y_{n,k_n} are independent and have mean zero. If the Lindeberg condition holds for every positive epsilon and the sum of their covariance matrices converges to Sigma, then the sum of the Y_{n,i} converges in distribution to N_k(0,Sigma).

attestation.note: Transcribed from van der Vaart, Asymptotic Statistics (Cambridge University Press, 1998), Theorem 2.27; publisher excerpt/source consulted. The cited iid finite-second-moment claim is the standard triangular-array specialization.
